text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament moves to 'arrest grabbing of public land' by approving a motion for the immediate review of the Government Lands Act and the establishment of district-based land commissions responsible for allocation.

- As a follow-up to President Daniel arap Moi's pledge to fully liberalise coffee and tea sectors, the government announces major changes that give growers power to elect directors who in turn will choose a chairman and chief executive.
- Two hard-core convicts at the Kwale Government prison in Coast Province stage a dramatic escape, leaving seven police officers and a prison warden seriously injured.
- Shock and disbelief leave thousands in tears throughout Kenya at news of the death of Minister of Research, Training and Applied Technology Dr Zachary Onyonka.

- American Ambassodor to Kenya Prudence Bushnell says her government plans to invest $100 million in Kenya during the next five years. This will largely depend on the Kenyan government's commitment to the democratisation process, economic reforms and good governance.
- Police officers who beat up Kitui Central deputy Charity Ngilu and two East African Standard journalists are suspended pending investigations.
- 1.03 million Kenyans are infected with the AIDS virus, with Nyanza Province leading among the country's eight provinces, says Assistant Health Minister Gideon Mutiso.
